subject: Mathematical Literacy
pacing_note: The IEB publishes no ATP equivalent; term placement and week spans are the DBE ATP pacing carried over as a default. IEB schools set their own pacing — treat weeks as advisory.
assessment_note: DBE SBA programmes, control-test scopes and exam structures are deliberately stripped: IEB assessment is specified by the IEB Subject Assessment Guidelines (see ../exam_guidelines/), which have not been ingested yet. Do not fall back to the CAPS exam_structure for IEB papers.

topics.name: PATTERNS AND RELATIONSHIPS
subtopics: Relationships (two at a time): constant difference, inverse proportion, constant ratio between consecutive terms, combinations
Representations: equations and formulae, dependent and independent variables, tables and graphs
Working with two relationships: compare tariff systems and banking options using formulae, equations, tables and graphs

topics.name: MEASUREMENTS
subtopics: Conversions: metric to imperial; temperature (°C to °F and back); time durations; equivalent-proportionality conversions (e.g. 5 l paint covers 20 m², 1 teaspoon ≈ 5 ml)
Measuring and estimating: length, distance, mass/weight, volume, temperature
Calculate perimeter, area (surface area) and volume; cost calculations may apply

topics.name: FINANCE
subtopics: Financial documents: terminology and calculating values on documents
Income (fixed, variable, occasional): personal (salaries, wages, commission) and business (sales, donations, grants) sources
Expenditure: personal (living expenses, personal tax, loan repayments) and business (taxes, salaries, running expenses)

topics.name: FINANCE
subtopics: Taxation: VAT, UIF
Exchange rates
Tariff systems: municipal, telephone, transport tariffs, bank fees; comparing two options via calculations and graphs

topics.name: MAPS, PLANS & OTHER REPRESENTATIONS
subtopics: Scales: number scales and bar scales
Maps (directions and point locations): seating plans, layout plans, street maps, national/provincial road and rail maps, residential maps

topics.name: DATA HANDLING
subtopics: Developing questions; collecting data: populations and samples, collection methods and instruments
Classifying and organising data: tallies and frequency tables
Summarising data: mean, median, mode, range; analysing the averages
Representing, interpreting and analysing: multiple bar graphs, line and broken-line graphs, scatter plots

topics.name: PROBABILITY
subtopics: Simple events: outcome, event and probability scale (revision); relative frequency; theoretical probability
Compound events: tree diagrams and two-way tables

topics.name: FINANCE
subtopics: Income, expenditure, profit and loss for large organisations and fundraising projects; two-year comparisons; projected vs actual budgets
Cost price and selling price: production/manufacturing cost, appropriate selling price, percentage profit
Break-even analysis: break-even values from formulae and graphs
Interest, loans and banking (calculate without formulae): loans, investments, bank accounts; savings, cheque/current, fixed deposit, credit and debit accounts
Inflation: calculation; rate of increase or decrease

topics.name: MAPS, PLANS & OTHER REPRESENTATIONS
subtopics: Building plans with scale: housing plans, elevation plans, design drawings
Models: packaging using actual cans and a range of boxes

topics.name: MAPS, PLANS & OTHER REPRESENTATIONS
subtopics: Assembling: following instructions (plugs, plastic models, flat-pack furniture, cell phones, electrical appliances, children's toys)

caps_notes: CAPS p.15: concepts must not be taught in the absence of contexts - learners must meet them in realistic scenarios
Requisite pre-knowledge across all terms: Grade 10 content
